snippet.title: Michael Jackson Trusted Him — Then the Interview Aired
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson trusted journalist Martin Bashir with unprecedented access to Neverland—but when *Living with Michael Jackson* aired, Michael called it a betrayal. This documentary examines how Bashir gained Michael Jackson’s trust, how the interview was edited, and how it changed the public’s view of him forever.

For eight months, Martin Bashir followed Michael Jackson through Neverland, hotel rooms and private moments with his children. Michael believed he was finally being given a chance to tell his story honestly. Instead, the broadcast became one of the most damaging moments of his life.

But Michael’s decision to trust Bashir was not as naive as it may appear.

Bashir was already famous for his interview with Princess Diana—the one interview that made Michael believe he could safely open up. Years later, an official inquiry revealed that Bashir had used forged documents and deception to secure Diana’s trust.

So was Michael Jackson targeted using the same playbook?

In this episode of The Recall, we revisit the making of *Living with Michael Jackson*, the footage Michael’s team recorded behind the scenes, the public backlash, the 2005 trial and the later revelations surrounding Martin Bashir’s interview methods.

Was Michael Jackson simply too trusting—or was the entire interview engineered from the beginning?

Share your opinion in the comments.

snippet.title: The Man Who Destroyed Michael Jackson..
snippet.description:
Did Martin Bashir destroy Michael Jackson, or did Michael's own trust in the camera do it? 🎥

In 2003, "Living with Michael Jackson" shocked the world. Months later came the Neverland raid, then the 2005 trial. Eighteen years later, the Lord Dyson report exposed how Bashir landed his Princess Diana interview. This video follows the full story, from the 1993 allegation to the "This Is It" tour that never happened, and asks who really built the image of Michael Jackson.

Martin Bashir 'used Princess Diana letter to land Michael Jackson interview' - new claims
FORMER BBC journalist Martin Bashir has been hit by fresh accusations in the wake of Lord Dyson's report into his 1995 Panorama interview with Princess Diana. 
Friends and family of Michael Jackson fear the reporter used rogue methods to secure a sitdown with the star.
Disgraced journalist Martin Bashir has been accused of using a letter of commendation from Princess Diana to secure an interview with mega pop star Michael Jackson. 
The singer's brother Tito and nephew Taj Jackson and close friend of Michael and Diana's, 
Uri Geller have aired their fears Mr Bashir hoodwinked Mr Jackson in the same way he did Diana.
Lord Dyson's report found Mr Bashir showed forged bank statements to Diana's brother Earl Spencer who later introduced the reporter to the princess.

The damning report highlighted the BBC's systematic failure to deal with Mr Bashir correctly 
and saw the organisation slammed by both Prince William, and Prince Harry, 36.

Now Michael Jackson's family and friends have accused Mr Bashir of using "unethical tactics" to land his infamous Neverland documentary with the star.
The singer's nephew Taj wrote online: “Bashir’s manipulated footage and unethical journalism is one of the main reasons my uncle is not here today."
He added: "That trial broke him. Shame on those who provided cover for Bashir. Shame on those who rewarded him. 
My family deserve an investigation and apology too.”

Michael's brother Tito claimed: “Bashir created a fake narrative about my brother, 
which becomes crystal clear when you view the out-takes Bashir kept secret.

"He used Michael’s trust and friendship with Diana to get the interview,
manipulated Michael throughout the interview, then deceptively edited the footage.”
Mutual friend of Diana and Michael, celebrity psychic Uri Geller claims Bashir produced a letter purportedly from Diana to gain access to Jackson, 
who was best man when he renewed his vows in 2001.

Mr Geller said it was this letter that convinced him to introduce Mr Bashir to Jackson.

He told the Mirror: “What convinced me to introduce him to Michael was a letter he pulled out of his pocket.

“It was folded two or three times and there was a logo on it.

snippet.title: MICHAEL JACKSON'S FURY: How the Media Betrayed the King of Pop
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson trusted journalist Martin Bashir with unprecedented access to his private life. When the documentary aired in 2003, the King of Pop was furious — and accused the interviewer of betrayal.

But Michael Jackson had something the public hadn't seen: footage from another camera.

In this documentary, we investigate one of the most explosive media controversies in Michael Jackson's career — and the interviews that led to it.

From Oprah Winfrey's revealing 1993 interview to Diane Sawyer's uncomfortable questions in 1995 and Barbara Walters' confrontation in 1997, Michael Jackson repeatedly found himself defending his personal life in front of millions.

Then came Martin Bashir.

For months, Bashir filmed Michael Jackson at Neverland Ranch and beyond. His documentary, Living with Michael Jackson, sparked international controversy and raised serious questions about the singer's conduct.

Jackson accused Bashir of misrepresenting him. Bashir denied those accusations.

When Michael's team released additional behind-the-scenes footage, viewers saw a striking contrast between Bashir's private praise and his critical documentary.

The controversy eventually became connected to the criminal proceedings against Jackson. In June 2005, Michael Jackson was acquitted on all counts.

This film explores the interviews, the hidden-camera controversy, the public response, and the complicated relationship between one of the world's biggest entertainers and the journalists who questioned him.

Was Michael Jackson betrayed by the media — or was the truth more complicated?

Watch the full documentary and decide for yourself.
